how: One source mutation applied to the working tree, the named suite run against it, then the file restored before the next row (X14/X15's convention: `before` is the shipped source the row was run against and `after` the text that replaced it, so `before` is findable verbatim in `file`). Device rows ran on lease G15-69l63, pair-a, on 2026-11-03; the `harness:android:Checkbox` / `harness:ios:Checkbox` runs are filtered, so they satisfy nothing but their own name. Rows marked `organic` are not mutations at all: they are the test going red against the real bug before the fix landed, which is the stronger evidence and is recorded here because the logs are the proof (`gate.mjs logs --branch task/G15-checkbox`).

redTests: the real tap that checks the box: 3 real presses on the controlled Checkbox (real-input-checkbox) left it at "off". Its own state never moved either, so on the evidence here the touch was never delivered (FOLLOWUPS.md:58)
mutations.note: The probe that read the tree in that same run said why: a press at the row's middle — over the label — changed nothing, a press on the glyph toggled, and a press at 0.20 of the row (still on the label) delivered nothing again. A switch-style Toggle hit-tests its glyph only, so the row got a tap target; the case is green on 365a0acb in 43.4s, with the event counter reaching exactly 1 then 2, which is what would go red on a double delivery.

mutations.mutation: drift the fixture: the controlled Checkbox's label goes from "Real input" to "x", moving the row's middle onto the glyph
redTests: the switch glyph starts at x=32.666666666666664 and the row's middle is at x=54.83333206176758 - a press at the middle has to land on the label's side of the glyph, or these taps prove nothing about the label
mutations.note: The row-tap fix is only worth what its aim is worth, so the aim is asserted before the first press: with the label this short the middle is over the box and the guard goes red, which is the fixture drift that would otherwise turn the case into a switch-only check.
